topic: OpenMausBot: Open Source Alternative to Grok Bot with a Virtual Machine

key_points: Official repo, Apache-2.0 license, 2.5k stars / 448 forks, 1,670 commits, active daily (latest commit hours before retrieval), v0.1.72.
Open-core: Apache-2.0 core with a source-available enterprise/ folder (delete it and the open-source edition still builds/runs).
Bring-your-own-agent: bots run on claude / codex / grok CLIs already installed on your machine — existing logins/subscriptions, no new accounts, no proxy.
Local-first: one harness server on 127.0.0.1:8799 owns every agent; transcripts, keys, events live in ~/.openmausbot.
Every bot gets a computer: cloud Linux desktop (Box API, box.ascii.dev), isolated Local VM, or — host control with explicit opt-in on macOS / Ubuntu Xorg (Wayland disabled for safety).
Composio marketplace for 500+ apps (Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear); permissions per-action via allow/deny cards (permission broker).
Chat-app metaphor: bots managed like contacts, channels per context, install a full team from one Markdown file via BotMRR import.

Clients: macOS (.dmg, signed/notarized), Windows (installer, unsigned - SmartScreen warning), Ubuntu 24.04 (.deb/AppImage beta, GNOME), iOS/Android companion; pair over Tailscale; self-host via npx openmausbot serve / Docker / podman.

Model picker with provider rail (Claude + Codex side by side), workspace provider API keys (Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible/xAI) for metered per-token billing, MCP server for orchestration (Claude Desktop/Cursor).
Crypto disclaimer: no token; any coin using the name is not affiliated.
Lists OpenMausBot as the closest direct Grok Bot clone: chat-app interface, per-bot model/memory/personality, running on cloud desktop, local VM, or your own machine.
Uses trycua/cua computer-use layer (MIT) underneath and Composio for integrations.
Grok Bot launched in beta Aug 11, 2026; open-source clones appeared within days.
Independent verification via git; OpenMausBot was 'active, 563 commits' at time of writing (Aug 2026).
Honest cost read: self-hosting trades subscription for infrastructure you run, metered API spend, maintenance, no SLA, and you own the security surface (credential storage, session isolation, audit).
Warns open-source clones are genuinely early with rough edges; expect unproven maintenance schedule.
Positioned as a comparison table of open-source Grok Bot alternatives: OpenMausBot 'gives each bot a virtual machine, local-first'.
Grok Bot facts: bundled with SuperGrok, SuperGrok Heavy, and Cursor Pro/Pro+/Ultra/Teams; each bot gets a cloud computer; closed source.
Contrast alternatives: Rakazo (any model + any sandbox, web/desktop/mobile), CopilotKit OpenBot (governance-first, AG-UI), gawkbot (one bot per workflow + microapp).
Emphasizes the category distinction: some clones focus on sandbox/VM, others on governance or outcomes.
Cautions buyers on licensing (source-available vs true open source) before adopting a clone.
OpenMausBot launched within hours of Grok Bot's release (Aug 2026) — 'shipped the open source version in hours'.
Runs on the Claude and Codex subscriptions you already have; every bot gets its own cloud computer you watch work live; signs into apps via Composio (500+ integrations).
Talks to agents like contacts in a messaging app, each with own personality/model/memory; asks before acting on risky actions; runs locally so data stays on your machine.
Frames the value prop vs $120/mo Grok Bot: free, local-first, your credentials/compute, and reuses existing subscriptions.
Milind S (author) posted: made an open-source Grok Bot without needing subscriptions, spins up VMs from ascii.dev, uses trycua for computer use.
Video: 'OpenMausBot: FREE Grok Bot Alternative!' — build a custom team of AI agents using your existing subscriptions.
Frames OpenMausBot as the practical, free, self-hosted path for teams that already pay for Claude/Codex.
Demonstrates the chat-driven agent workflow rather than a vendor bundle.

stats.fact: OpenMausBot GitHub repo: 2.5k+ stars, 448 forks, 1,670+ commits; latest commit hours before research on Sep 10, 2026; latest release v0.1.72 (Sep 10, 2026).
Grok Bot launched in beta on August 11, 2026; open-source clones appeared within days of launch.
OpenMausBot is Apache 2.0 licensed (open-core with a source-available enterprise/ folder that can be deleted to leave a pure open-source edition).
Bots reuse existing claude / codex / grok CLI subscriptions and logins — no new accounts, no proxy in the middle; custom CLI binaries supported via Settings → Engines.

Each bot gets its own computer: cloud Linux desktop (Box API, box.ascii.dev), isolated Local VM, or host computer with explicit opt-in (macOS / Ubuntu Xorg; Ubuntu Wayland host control disabled as a safety gate).
500+ app integrations through Composio (Gmail, Slack, GitHub, Notion, Linear, and more).
Grok Bot is bundled with SuperGrok, SuperGrok Heavy, and Cursor paid plans; open-source alternatives remove the vendor bundle requirement.
OpenMausBot uses the trycua/cua computer-use layer (MIT) underneath plus Composio for third-party app integrations.

angles: The speed of open-source commoditization: a Grok-Bot-scale product rebuilt and shipped within hours/days of xAI's August 11, 2026 launch — 'the speed of open source is genuinely terrifying'.
Bring-your-own-agent economics: reuse the Claude/Codex/grok subscriptions you already pay for instead of a new $120/mo (or SuperGrok/Cursor) bundle.
Local-first privacy vs hosted convenience: transcripts, keys, and events stay in ~/.openmausbot on your machine; your credentials and compute never route through a vendor cloud.

Real security/cost trade-offs: self-hosting means you own credential storage, session isolation, audit logs, metered API spend, and maintenance with no vendor SLA — clones are early (1,670 commits but project days/weeks old) and the Ubuntu Wayland host-control gate is a real limitation.

Category map: OpenMausBot (VM/computer focus) vs Rakazo (any model + sandbox, web/desktop/mobile) vs CopilotKit OpenBot (governance-first AG-UI) vs gawkbot (per-workflow microapps) — pick by what you're optimizing.
The VM story: cloud desktop (Box/ascii.dev) vs Local VM vs your own machine, with per-action approval cards making every risky action a decision you make.
